readall_conflicts: No source says anything about word stress, so there is no disagreement on stress. The sources do disagree on tone by variety: Lüpke 2005 (thesis, pp. 84-87) shows with pitch tracks and comprehension experiments that the Jalonke of Saare Kindia, Guinea, has no lexical or grammatical tone, while Creissels 1989 (p. 20), Creissels 2010 and Keita 1987/88, 1989 describe the Dialonké of Faléya, Mali, as a two-register tone language (H/B) with elaborate tone-realisation rules; Lüpke herself notes the difference and treats it as tone loss in the Guinean variety. The listed work (Lüpke 2005, LDD 3) is a corpus-methodology article and is silent on both stress and tone.

sources.citation: Creissels, Denis. 2010. Liste lexicale du dialonké de Faléya. Mandenkan 46: 49-71.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Tone-marked wordlist; intro (pp. 49-50) says Lüpke's variety 'diffère essentiellement du dialonké de Faléya par la perte des distinctions tonales notées dans ce lexique', and that only heavy syllable rhymes can bear BH/HB sequences. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Lüpke, Friederike. 2005. Small is beautiful: contributions of field-based corpora to different linguistic disciplines, illustrated by Jalonke. LDD 3: 75-105.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Open-access article that reuses the tone experiments; could contain a prosodic characterisation (stress/intonation) absent from the thesis; blocked only by a bot wall.

sources.citation: Creissels, Denis. 1989. Structures syllabiques du dialonké de Faléya. Mandenkan 18: 1-30.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Dialonké of Faléya (Kéniéba, Mali) is tonal: 'Le dialonké a un système tonal réductible à deux unités tonologiques de base, |H| et |B|' (p. 20, §7); CV syllables carry one tone, CV:/CVC syllables may carry HB or BH; tone-realisation rules (H-spreading, lowering) described pp. 20-28. No statement about stress/accent in Dialonké; 'accentuation' is mentioned only for Latin/Arabic as a comparison (p. 20).

sources.citation: Keita, Boniface. 1989. La compacité tonale en dialonké. Mandenkan 18: 205-215.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Tonal compactness (tone of compound/genitive constructions) in Dialonké; floating tones, H/B schemes. Nothing on stress or accent (scanned, English model; image-only PDF).
